compute.note: parameters = np = iesm + iesd + iesh + (iback(1..4)) + iesfree + iessw + iesup + ieskin = 0 + 14 + 0 + 4 + 1 + 0 + 0 + 1 = 20 variational parameters (the code's own formula, Main_uniform_wf.f), matching the 20 optimised values listed in datprep.d after the namelists (Jastrow, backflow, pairing/field and chemical-potential terms, in the order the code reads them; &nelectrons nelup=28 neldo=36; one determinant of backflow orbitals per configuration). The script does NOT optimise: datasvmc.d sets itestr=2 ("VMC", measurement with the fixed parameters read from datprep.d; itestr=-2 is the minimiser) and the program README says the input files contain "the optimal variational parameters". The run it scripts is one measurement of ngen = 2000000 Monte Carlo generations of nbra = 64 = N single-electron proposals each (one walker, nw=1), from which Energy.x takes bins of 1000 and drops the first 5. The &optimization namelist in the same file (nweight=5000 generations per SR step, ibinit=50, tau=0.02) is not read at itestr=2, and no file states how many optimisation steps produced the parameters, so samples and iterations (per optimisation step, and optimisation steps) are null. Doubt: the Fortran as committed is compiled for nx=45, L=270 (Main_uniform_wf.f parameter statement), so for this 64-site instance the program must be edited and recompiled before the script can run. Searched for the optimisation run: the script, both input files, programs/vmc_hubbard (README, Main_*/Prep_* sources), the VarBench data file and Hubbard/supplements (Imada_group_overview.md, AFQMC.md), the VarBench paper (arXiv:2302.04919, Sec. S3 on VMC). No time is recorded anywhere.

compute.reported_as: arXiv:1505.02290 (LeBlanc et al., PRX 5, 041041), Sec. II B AFQMC: The second approach we employ, to treat cases where the sign problem does occur, is referred to as the constrained path Monte Carlo method. [...] Both methods obtain the ground state of the Hamiltonian for a supercell of size L x L under twist-averaged boundary conditions. [...] The total projection length is typically beta = 64 in the ground state projection method, although test calculations with imaginary-time lengths several times larger were performed. [...] In the constrained path method, the runs are open-ended and tend to correspond to much larger values of beta. [...] Most calculations reported here use a time-step fixed at Delta tau = 0.01 in units of t. [...] For small systems a large number of Theta values are needed (~200 for 4 x 4 or 6 x 6), but for larger systems, far fewer Theta are required [...] || arXiv:1307.2147 (Shi & Zhang, PRB 88, 125132), Sec. III A (a different 8 x 8 run, N_up = N_dn = 13, U = 4, free projection): The run took ~17 hours on 100 AMD Opteron 2.4GHz cores. [...] Fig. 3/4 captions: The number of walkers was 10^5 [...] The number of walkers is 5 x 10^5, with total 100 separate runs to estimate the error bars. || arXiv:2308.08594 (the citing paper) states nothing about the cost of its refs [17, 18].
compute.source: arXiv:1505.02290 Sec. II B (AFQMC method) and Tables IV-V; arXiv:1307.2147 Sec. III A, Fig. 3-4 captions, Tables I-II; arXiv:2308.08594 (citing paper, Sec. I-III), arXiv:1505.02290 (compute pass 2026-09-16)
compute.note: Neither original paper states a cost for this 8 x 8 constrained-path AFQMC energy: the finite-size 8 x 8 doped entries (N = 50 and 56 electrons) are in the supplemental data sets of LeBlanc et al., whose main text gives only the generic AFQMC settings (projection length typically beta = 64 for the ground-state projection method, open-ended for constrained path; Delta tau = 0.01; twist averaging), and Shi & Zhang's tables (their Tables I-II) do not contain these fillings at all. The only concrete run-time statement in either paper (~17 hours on 100 AMD Opteron 2.4 GHz cores, 5 x 10^5 walkers x 100 runs) is for a different 8 x 8 free-projection benchmark (N_up = N_dn = 13, U = 4) in Shi & Zhang and is not attributed to this row. The citing paper arXiv:2308.08594 quotes the numbers without cost information. Both originals fetched: fetched/1307.2147.pdf/.txt (pdftotext reported a repairable xref error; text extracted), fetched/1505.02290.pdf/.txt.

compute.reported_as: Our implementation utilizes Jax [29] to perform automatic differentiation and sampling, alongside the Optax package [30] for optimization. (...) Optimization generally uses around 180 optimization steps with varying and decaying step size (see appendix); gradients are accumulated with 189,000 samples and parameters are updated using a random step with the computed sign [11]. || After optimization, parameters are selected based on the lowest observed average energy. Using this parameter set, observables such as the local energy and electron occupation are measured with approximately 10^6 samples with a thermalization of 10^3 sweeps. || Most of these parameters are in T_l^sigma, with O(N_l * N^2) parameters. || The step sizes during the first 79 steps of optimization is 0.01 and then is lowered to 0.001 for the remaining 100 steps. The optimal point is selected by the lowest energy during the optimization, normally somewhere after the first 80 steps. Optimization was performed with 126 independent walkers contributing to the total sample collection, while the additional measurement of the optimized parameters used 120 walkers. Each measurement was collected after N * N_l Metropolis updates and values reported in the main text were averaged over walkers and a 1000 sweep thermalization time was used. (...) Variance measurement was performed with an additional 10x samples.
compute.source: Sec. II A Implementation Details; Sec. II (parameter scaling); Appendix A Further Computational Details, arXiv:2308.08594 (compute pass 2026-09-16) (compute pass 2026-09-24)
compute.note: Blanket statements for all VAFQMC (N_l = 4) results; nothing is given per system size. samples = the "approximately 10^6 samples" used for the final energy measurement; gradients during optimization used 189,000 samples per step; 126 walkers (optimization) / 120 walkers (measurement); 1000-sweep thermalization; variance measured with 10x more samples. iterations = "around 180 optimization steps" (79 at step size 0.01 + 100 at 0.001 per Appendix A). Parameter count not stated, only the scaling O(N_l * N^2), dominated by the T_l^sigma hopping matrices. No hardware, GPU/CPU-hours or wall-clock stated anywhere (JAX + Optax implementation; affiliation Flatiron Institute, no machine named). || route2b-pass 2026-09-24: Parameters: only the scaling is stated ("Most of these parameters are in T_l^sigma, with O(N_l * N^2) parameters"; alpha = {lambda_i, tau_l^sigma, t_l^sigma_ij}, T_l not Hermitian). Not countable: whether T_l^sigma is a dense N x N matrix, whether lambda_i is per slice, and whether |phi_0> is optimised are not stated. Searched: arXiv v2 (= PRR 6, 013237 text, Sections II-III, Appendices A-B), GitHub (no code by the authors; icf/vafqmc_afqmc is unrelated). DISAGREEMENT with the stored samples: the paper states "gradients are accumulated with 189,000 samples" per optimisation step; the stored samples = 1e6 is the post-optimisation measurement ("measured with approximately 10^6 samples"). Kept as stored; per DATA.md (samples per optimisation step) the value should be 189,000. VAFQMC is not a network: a cost model needs N_l = 4 slices, the k = 3 product formula for exp(T), the O(N_l N^3) per-sample cost, 126 walkers x N N_l Metropolis updates per measurement, 189,000 samples x 180 steps. || Ruling 2026-09-24 (Tristan): samples = 189000 per optimisation step as the quoted sentence states; the stored 1e6 was the measurement count.
